reasoning: The Acme Bank AI Governance Policy (ACME-POL-AIGOV-002, Section 5) requires a Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment that documents intended purpose, data quality, known limitations, fairness/bias considerations, and sign-off for high-impact systems. Section 4 establishes the AIGC as the approval body for high-impact systems and Section 2 confirms the policy applies to all production AI. These fragments therefore touch the same underlying obligation (governance and risk-management for high-risk AI) and provide partial organisational controls (pre-deployment assessment and governance sign-off). However, none of the retrieved fragments explicitly require or describe the specific technical and organisational measures the Article 15(4) obligation demands to ensure resilience against errors, faults or inconsistencies — e.g., fault-tolerance or redundancy designs, robustness/adversarial testing, runtime monitoring and alerting for errors/inconsistencies, automated rollback/fallback procedures, incident response and recovery processes, or ongoing post-deployment resilience testing. A human Compliance Analyst should review and either confirm that ACME-POL-AIGOV-002 Section 5 (and related sections) are sufficient or identify where additional explicit requirements for technical resilience and operational controls must be added.

retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
Before any AI system is deployed to production, the owning business unit must
complete a Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment covering:

- Intended purpose and use cases
- Data sources and data quality
- Known limitations of the model or system
- Fairness and bias considerations
- Sign-off from the AIGC for high-impact systems

The AI Governance Committee (AIGC) meets monthly and is the approval body for any
AI system classified as "high impact" under the Acme Bank AI Risk Tiering
Framework (see Section 5).

Applies to all AI systems used in production, including those developed in-house
and those procured from third parties, across all business lines.
